concepts.title: What is Mathematics: The Search for Patterns
concepts.definition: Mathematics is largely the search for patterns and for explanations of why those patterns exist, whether in nature, in homes and schools, or in the motion of the sun, moon and stars.
concepts.key_idea: Spotting a pattern is only half the work; explaining why it must continue is the mathematical part.

concepts.title: Square Numbers from Odd Numbers
concepts.definition: Adding consecutive odd numbers, 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + ..., builds up square numbers: the sum of the first n odd numbers is the n-th square, and the pictures of dots make the rule visible.
concepts.key_idea: Odd numbers are the stair-steps of squares: each new odd number grows the square by one new L-shaped border.

solution_steps.explain: Adding 1 + 3 + ... up to n odd numbers equals n times n.

concepts.title: Triangular Number Rule
concepts.definition: Triangular numbers 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 count counters stacked as triangles: the n-th triangular number is 1 + 2 + ... + n, which equals n times (n + 1) divided by 2.
concepts.key_idea: Two identical triangles of counters combine into an n by (n + 1) rectangle, which halves into the rule.

solution_steps.explain: Write the running sums 1, 3, 6, 10 as the triangular pattern.
Multiply n by one more than n and take half.

concepts.title: Patterns in Shapes and Their Number Relations
concepts.definition: Shape sequences, regular polygons growing from triangle to square to pentagon, or nested squares and triangles, carry number sequences inside them: counting sides, matches or regions turns shape patterns into number patterns.
concepts.key_idea: Every shape pattern hides a number sequence, and every number sequence can be drawn as shapes.
